title: Publish narrow contracts for prepared-media reuse and virtual presentations
finding: Engine preparation already shares immutable assets and preview work has separate owners. R018 owns source/recipe prepared-media caching and the unified study owns engine sharing. Neither is evidence for sharing live parsers or clocks between export and playback.
novelty: Merge into R018; retain engine-sharing links without counting their savings again or inventing a universal graph.
next_action: When a repeated-preparation workload warrants integration, key reuse by immutable source, selected tracks, recipe, metadata epoch, destination and runtime; test individual invalidations and consumer cancellation, then charge retained memory and cold preparation.
reopen_condition: This is not a license to construct a universal graph engine. Reuse existing R018/mpv/FFmpeg facilities first; stop if bookkeeping exceeds saved preparation.

proposal_contract.Proposed mechanism: Separate source identity, selected tracks, transform recipe, metadata epoch and destination representation in reusable prepared state. Share immutable work while keeping live parser/decoder clocks independent.
proposal_contract.Smallest useful experiment: Open the same source for playback, preview and export; vary one track, recipe or destination at a time. Force cancellation of one consumer and source identity change.
proposal_contract.Correctness gate: Reuse only when dependencies match, no stale timeline state, original payload checks pass, and selected owners remain isolated through failure.
proposal_contract.Measure only after correctness: Repeated preparation, distinct assets/compilations and source reads, with retained-memory and invalidation cost.

upstream_evidence: Imported 2026-09-21 source review, not fetched or revalidated in this run.
